summary: The change turns the search page into a client component. The component reads q from the URL, fetches matching products and lists them.

findings.title: URL query rendered as raw HTML
findings.problem: The heading injects the q search parameter into dangerouslySetInnerHTML without escaping or sanitizing it.
findings.consequence: An attacker can send a crafted /search?q= link that runs script in the victim's session. This is reflected XSS.
findings.fix: Render the query as a normal JSX text child so React escapes it.

findings.title: Effect without dependencies refetches forever
findings.problem: The useEffect has no dependency array, so it runs after every render. Each run calls setResults with a new array, which triggers another render.
findings.consequence: The page sends search requests to /api/products in an endless loop. This loads the API and the browser.
findings.fix: Pass [query] as the dependency array so the effect runs only when the query changes.

findings.title: Hooks called after a conditional return
findings.problem: SearchPage returns early when q is missing, before it calls useState and useEffect. The hook count then differs between renders.
findings.consequence: React throws a rendered-more-hooks error when q changes from empty to set on the same mounted page. The search page crashes.
findings.fix: Call useState and useEffect before the early return. Skip the fetch inside the effect when query is empty.

findings.title: Search form removed with no replacement
findings.problem: The change deletes the only search form in the repository. The empty state asks the user to type a term, but the page offers no input.
findings.consequence: Users cannot start a search from the UI. Only a hand-edited URL reaches results.
findings.fix: Keep the form with the q input on the page, at least in the empty state.

findings.title: Search failure is never handled
findings.problem: searchProducts throws when the response is not ok, and the effect attaches no catch handler. The rejected promise floats.
findings.consequence: A failed search causes an unhandled rejection. The user sees an empty list with no error message.
findings.fix: Add a catch handler that stores an error state and renders a message.

findings.title: List items lack a key
findings.problem: The results map renders each li without a key prop. Product has a stable id field that the map could use.
findings.consequence: React logs a warning and cannot reconcile the list correctly when results change.
findings.fix: Set key to product.id on each li.

findings.title: New search behaviour has no test
findings.problem: SearchPage now has an empty-query branch, a fetch and a results list. No test covers any of them.
findings.consequence: Regressions in the search page can ship without notice.
findings.fix: Add a component test for the empty query, a successful search and a failed search.
